# Reading Tutor Cost vs. Reading Apps: An Honest Comparison

It's back-to-school season, and if your child came home from kindergarten or first grade behind on reading, you're probably weighing two options: hire a private tutor, or try a reading app. The honest answer is that these aren't really competitors — they solve different problems at very different price points. Here's how to think about it clearly, without the sales pitch from either side.

## What a private reading tutor actually costs

In the US, private reading tutors typically charge $40-80 per hour, depending on region and credentials. Specialized tutors trained in structured literacy approaches like Orton-Gillingham — often the right fit for dyslexia or other diagnosed reading difficulties — frequently charge at the top of that range or higher, sometimes $90-120/hr in major metro areas. A once-a-week session adds up to roughly $160-350 a month; twice a week, which is common for kids working through a real deficit, can run $350-700+ a month.

That price buys you something an app genuinely cannot: a trained adult who watches your child read in real time, diagnoses exactly which sounds or patterns are tripping them up, and adjusts instruction session to session. # Private reading tutor: what parents need to know before hiring

Private reading tutors cost $40, $120/hr and can accelerate progress. Learn who to hire, what methods work, and when the school must pay instead.

ReadFlare Team July 9, 2026 28 min read

In This Article

Last updated 2026-07-09

Adult tutor and young child working together at a sunlit wooden table

## TL;DR

A private reading tutor works one-on-one with a struggling reader using structured, systematic methods. Expect to pay $40, $120 per hour depending on credentials and location. Tutors with Orton-Gillingham or structured literacy training get the strongest results for kids with dyslexia. If your child has an IEP, the school may be legally required to provide reading intervention at no cost, so know your rights before you pay out of pocket.

## What does a private reading tutor actually do?

A private reading tutor works with one child at a time, usually for 45 to 60 minutes per session, targeting the specific skills that child is missing. That's the key distinction from classroom instruction: there's no group to pace to, no competing demands. The tutor can slow down on phoneme blending if that's the gap, or push harder on fluency if decoding is solid but reading sounds robotic.
